title: Normalize role delimiters and canonicalize tokenization during model onboarding
creator: Ana Martinez
description:
Background:
During onboarding of new chat-capable open models we observed inconsistent token counts between the model's tokenizer and Redwood's chat template normalization. In a handful of cases this produced off-by-one tokenization for role delimiters (e.g., <|assistant|> vs Assistant:), which cascaded into incorrect prefix caching, KV cache misalignment, and regressions in latency and quality for streamed responses.

Goal:
Ensure the onboarding pipeline canonicalizes role delimiters and tokenizer metadata for every model variant, publish a deterministic performance profile that accounts for canonicalization, and pin onboarding artifacts so downstream customers get consistent behavior across host/dedicated/private deployments.

Proposed approach:
1) Add a normalization stage in the onboarding pipeline that maps common chat role delimiters to a canonical delimiter set and records the mapping in model metadata (tokenizer_normalization_v1). This stage runs before performance profiling and compatibility tests.
2) Extend tokenizer metadata produced during onboarding to include: canonical_delimiters (list), delimiter_token_ids (example mapping), last_trained_tokenizer_hash, and tokenizer_normalization_version. Store these as strings in the model catalog entry so the console and SDK can surface them.
3) Implement a deterministic validation test that runs sample system/user/assistant templates through both the model tokenizer and Redwood's canonicalizer, asserting identical token sequences. Fail onboarding if mismatch cannot be resolved by normalization and add a soft-fail mode that flags the model for manual review.
4) When publishing performance profiles, include tokenization differences (tokens_per_role) so cost/latency estimates reflect canonicalized token counts. Publish a short note on model page indicating the normalization applied.
5) Add an onboarding flag to pin tokenizer_normalization_version and tokenizer_hash to a specific model version to prevent silent changes in hosted/dedicated/private flows.

Trade-offs and considerations:
- Backwards compatibility: Changing canonical delimiters could alter token counts for existing customers. We will not rewrite existing active catalog entries; instead we will surface the change and offer an opt-in migration path for customers to re-pin to the new canonicalization.
- Complexity vs safety: A permissive normalization may hide tokenizer bugs; a strict policy will block borderline models. We will ship permissive normalization + manual review for P1 models, strict enforcement for P0/customer-facing enterprise models.

Implementation tasks (rough):
- [ENG] Add tokenizer_normalizer module and unit tests (Kofi)
- [ENG] Hook normalization into onboarding pipeline pre-profile (Kofi + Maya)
- [ENG] Extend catalog metadata schema + DB migration script (Sujata)
acceptance_criteria:
1) Onboarding pipeline produces a model catalog entry with tokenizer_normalization_version and canonical_delimiters filled.
2) Deterministic validation test passes for five canonical chat templates across encoder/decoder model types.
3) Performance profile metrics include tokens_per_role and match canonicalized counts.
4) A manual review mode exists and is documented in the onboarding playbook.
